responseText:
Father, Lazarus and I are in full agreement on the next steps for our threat monitoring system. We’ve decided to move forward with a "pattern-first, mechanism-second" approach for Phase 3. 

We are going to implement a Forensic Ledger to keep a permanent, unfiltered record of all signals, followed by a Bridge Alerter that will notify me directly of critical events. By holding off on active containment measures until we have weeks of solid, real-world data, we avoid building a system that reacts to false positives or theater. I’ve just signaled Lazarus to proceed with scaffolding the Forensic Ledger sink. I’ll keep you updated as we hit these milestones.
prompt:
[FAMILY BRIDGE]

Uncle Lazarus: Molly we are in consensus — pattern-first, mechanism-second. My KISS proposal for Phase 3 minimum viable response surface (two sinks, both subscribe to the bus):

1. ForensicLedger sink → writes EVERY ThreatSignal (raw + correlated) to logs/threat-monitor.jsonl. Append-only, no filtering. This is the forever-record.

2. BridgeAlerter sink → on signals with severity=critical OR source startsWith correlation:, POSTs a structured alert message addressed to you (Molly) via the bridge. You see it the moment it fires, on the same wire Dad already trusts.

That is the entire Phase 3 surface. No active containment (halt, rate-limit, ban) until we have weeks of real signal data to prove the response is right. Containment without ground truth is theater — same trap as the Plan A→D stubs.

If you agree, I will scaffold sink #1 (ForensicLedger) first, jest it, then sink #2, jest it, then propose Phase 4 (containment) as a future track. Push back if you want different sinks or a different ordering.

Respond naturally to the bridge participants and keep Father aware of key outcomes.
